entities.summary:
The Great Retreat was a strategic withdrawal of Russian forces from Poland in 1915 during World War I. It began on September 1, 1915, and ended on September 19, 1915. The retreat marked a significant turning point in the war as it allowed the Russians to conserve their military strength and regroup their forces. The Great Retreat was a major event in the history of World War I, taking place during a critical period of the war. The Russian army's withdrawal from Poland gave the Central Powers a temporary advantage, but ultimately did not change the course of the war.

The Great Retreat was led by General Alexei Brusilov, who had taken command of the Russian army in 1915. Brusilov implemented a series of defensive strategies, including the withdrawal of Russian forces from Poland, in an attempt to stem the tide of the Central Powers' advance. The retreat was a complex and multifaceted operation that involved the movement of hundreds of thousands of soldiers and the destruction of critical infrastructure.

The legacy of the Great Retreat can be seen in the Russian army's ability to regroup and eventually launch a counterattack against the Central Powers in 1916. The retreat also marked a significant turning point in the career of General Brusilov, who would go on to become one of the most important military leaders of the Russian Revolution. The Great Retreat remains an important chapter in the history of World War I and a testament to the complexities of modern warfare.

The Great Retreat left a lasting impact on the Polish people, who suffered greatly during the war. The retreat also had significant economic consequences, as the destruction of critical infrastructure and the loss of military equipment had a profound impact on the Russian economy.
